data.description:
Operator's TOP concern from the Trident review (notes/trident-review-mailbox-feature-pack-20260615-2208/synthesis-evolutionary.md §8). Today the stdin handler pastes a framed <c11-msg> block into the recipient PTY and dispatches Return — unsafe when the agent is mid-command or in a raw-mode app (Vim): corrupts the input stream. Gemini predicts operators abandon stdin delivery within 3 months unless this is fixed.

Deliverable (two layers, both reuse existing machinery — minimize new hooks):
1. Gate the push on c11's ALREADY-tracked PanelShellActivityState { unknown, promptIdle, commandRunning } (Workspace.swift:5399, already used for close-confirmation). In StdinMailboxHandler: promptIdle -> inject now; commandRunning -> BUFFER and flush on transition back to promptIdle; unknown -> conservative buffer. No new lifecycle hook.
2. Add a receiver-pull cadence to the c11 skill (agents 'c11 mailbox recv --drain' at turn boundaries) as the robust floor — the AgentMail-style pull pattern. Zero c11 code; sync installed skill.

Validation: dogfood test — fire messages into agents mid-Vim and mid-build on a tagged build, confirm no PTY corruption and that buffered messages flush at the next prompt. This test also empirically settles the Claude-vs-Gemini split on whether PTY delivery is safe.

Scope guard: NOT the full out-of-band control-socket (that pushes a listener into the agent layer — bigger than 'minimize hooks'). Revisit only if the prompt-gate proves insufficient in the dogfood test.
data.title: Mailbox: delivery safety — prompt-gated stdin injection + receiver-pull cadence

data.body: Headless code-review: PASS (art_01KV7A8RDW3995J4VKWS7QC87T). CRITICAL finding was a review-harness packaging defect (it was handed the #251/#252 diff, not C11-144; reviewer worked around it by reviewing the actual branch 5c9cbe70e..HEAD). MAJOR = the live dogfood gate, doing now. Actioned MINOR: added logStdinLifecycle trace test. Noted tradeoffs: residual flush-onto-bare-shell within the 600s window near agent-exit (acknowledged design limit, dogfood will probe), and #252's positional %@ localization issue (out of scope, already merged).

PR open: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/254 (base main, NOT merged). Live validation PASS (artifact art_01KV7B4SA3RTY5DNVEYGCHYYXC): all gate paths confirmed end-to-end; gated send left vim pristine, raw ungated push corrupted vim — empirically settles the Claude-vs-Gemini split (ungated PTY push IS unsafe; the gate fixes it). Headline design realization: Layer 1 (gate) is a SAFETY mechanism, Layer 2 (recv --drain cadence) is the DELIVERY contract — a live agent TUI stays commandRunning its whole life so push into it always buffers and relies on pull. Flagged a pre-existing infra bug (CMUX_TAB_ID exported as surface UUID, not workspace UUID → shell-state reports dropped at scope resolution → state stuck unknown); recommend a separate follow-up ticket. Not in C11-144 scope.

Filed follow-up C11-147 (bug) for the pre-existing shell-state-reporting issue (CMUX_TAB_ID==surface UUID breaks report_shell_state scope resolution). Until that lands, C11-144's push-flush relies on the Layer-2 recv --drain pull cadence (which is the delivery contract anyway).

Merged as PR #254 (squash f4c2b4c69). Prompt-gated stdin delivery + buffer/flush via PanelShellActivityState; live-validated (gated vim pristine, ungated corrupted). C11-147 filed as follow-up. CI green.
